text:
Pierre-Luc Dubois is healthy again after a 2025-26 limited to 29 games, and after an October illness cost him a stretch of games, he has found the net. He has scored in four straight, twice against New Jersey, and has 12 points in 13 games.

Plenty of that is real. At five-on-five Washington gets almost 58% of the expected goals with him on the ice (expected goals measure the quality of chances), 6 points better than without him. But the finishing is running well ahead of the chances: 5 goals on 2.7 expected, shooting 22.7% against a range for him that tops out near 17%. The Capitals have also scored 6.1 more goals than their chances deserve with him out there. On-ice luck like that fades, so expect the goal streak to be the part that cools, not the play.

Evolving-Hockey had him facing competition in the 98th percentile last season, from a small sample. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, from just seven games, had him carrying the puck in on 71% of his entries. None of his points have come on the power play. Watch his five-on-five share; that's the part of his game worth trusting.
headline: Dubois is scoring, and the bounces are helping
